w10_T4_008926: Marcus had 106 dollars in his savings account in the morning. By afternoon, he had quadrupled his money through smart investments. That evening, he gave 46 dollars to his sister Sarah as a gift. The next day, Marcus received 19 dollars in cash from his uncle. He then multiplied his total by 6 when calculating his projected annual savings. Finally, he paid 1253 dollars toward his car loan and received 8 dollars in refund. How much money does Marcus have now?
w10_T4_008930: A bookshop received 68 copies of a new bestseller. The manager doubled the order to prepare for a sale. Then 47 more copies arrived as a bonus shipment. The store multiplied all its stock by 6 to plan for a regional expansion. On opening day, they sold 25 copies to eager customers. The remaining inventory was multiplied by 9 for an online listing. A visiting author had signed 156 books the week before, but that inventory was separate. How many books does the shop now have for sale?
w10_T4_008932: Emma started with 22 beads for her jewelry project. She multiplied her collection by 5 after a shopping trip. Her friend gave her 36 more beads as a gift. Emma then acquired 75 additional beads from a craft fair. She doubled her total collection for safekeeping. Finally, she used 298 beads to make bracelets as gifts. Compared to her friend Sarah, who had half as many beads as Emma started with, how many does Emma have left?
w10_T4_008940: A farm had 120 acres of farmland. The owner multiplied the planted area by 4 to expand operations. Then 7 additional acres were cleared for new crops. The farm's productive land was multiplied by 3 as they added irrigation. After a good harvest season, they added 60 more acres to the working area. By year-end, they multiplied the total by 7 for their annual report. Then 58 acres were set aside for conservation. What is the total number of acres under active cultivation?
w10_T4_008945: A bakery had 44 loaves at the start of the day. The baker multiplied production by 6 to meet weekend demand. Throughout the morning, customers added 67 loaves to special orders. Another 57 loaves arrived from a partner bakery. Then 35 more custom loaves were requested. Finally, 13 additional loaves came from a delivery. The baker counted 18 loaves reserved for a catering event that were not included in today's total. How many loaves are available after tripling the amount for Monday's planning?
w10_T4_008948: A parking lot started with 78 spaces. They added 71 new spaces in an expansion. Then the lot was reconfigured 4 times, multiplying effective capacity each time. After the second reconfiguration, they had 4 times the original expanded capacity. Then they lost 1274 spaces due to a zoning restriction and gained 13 back in negotiation. Finally, they multiplied the remaining spaces by 9 for a special event parking plan. How many effective spaces did the plan account for, given that the event parking needs increased their workload?
w10_T4_008953: A grocery store had 29 packs of milk in stock. They subtracted 16 packs when moving to a new display. Then they multiplied their stock by 8 to prepare for a promotion. Another multiplication by 5 occurred when they combined two store inventories. Finally, they divided the total by 5 to create equal portions for five departments. What is the final amount each department receives?
w10_T4_008955: A baker had 229 ounces of flour. They multiplied it by 8 to calculate their bulk supply. Then they used 29 ounces for a large wedding cake. The remaining flour was doubled for a month-long projection. Finally, 43 ounces were added as new stock. Comparing the baker's flour to their assistant's (who had half the original amount), how many ounces does the baker end up with?
w10_T4_008957: A textile factory received 207 meters of fabric. They doubled the inventory by 8 when receiving shipments twice. Then 553 meters were used in production. Finally, they tripled the remaining stock by 3 for quarterly reporting. A different warehouse had 150 meters in cold storage, which was not part of this calculation. In hours rather than meters, how much fabric remains when converted to processing time?
w10_T4_008971: A library had 147 books initially. They multiplied the collection by 9 through donations. Then they multiplied again by 9 when expanding to branches. After cataloging, 3574 books required repairs and were set aside. Then 48 books were returned in good condition. In terms of availability rather than quantity, what is the final count of books ready for checkout?
w10_T4_008972: A warehouse started with 71 boxes. They multiplied by 8 when loading shipments. Then by 6 again for a larger truck route. Then by 9 for a full regional distribution center count. After assembly, 8 boxes were damaged and removed. A major loss of 16132 boxes occurred due to a delivery error. Finally, they multiplied the remaining inventory by 9. How many boxes remained in their system for tracking purposes?
w10_T4_008977: A farmer had 63 baskets of apples. They multiplied by 7 during harvest season. They added 76 more baskets from neighboring farms. Then they subtracted 454 baskets sold at market. The remaining stock was multiplied by 7 for storage planning. Finally, 10 baskets were added as they found them in storage. In terms of days of production rather than baskets, what is the farmer's adjusted count?
w10_T4_008979: A tailor had 49 meters of fabric. They multiplied by 6 when restocking. Then added 67 meters from a supplier. They subtracted 91 meters for large orders. Then subtracted 111 meters for another client project. Finally, subtracted 118 meters for alterations and the remaining stock. Considering that double the original amount would be typical for the season, how much fabric does the tailor have now?
w10_T4_008980: A restaurant started with 82 dinner plates. They added 38 plates during an equipment order. Then multiplied the total by 5 for event planning. Then by 6 for a hotel contract. They divided everything by 3 to allocate to three shifts. Finally, 56 additional plates arrived. How many plates are allocated between Sarah (who manages the restaurant) and James (who oversees supplies)?
w10_T4_008990: A store had 235 items in inventory. They added 10 more items. Then subtracted 123 items sold during a sale. The remaining stock was divided in half for two warehouse locations. Finally, 12 items arrived as restocking. One nearby location had 98 items, but that was not included in this count. After converting to dollars, what is the final inventory count?
w10_T4_008999: A photographer had 62 digital files. They subtracted 27 corrupted files. Then subtracted 17 more that were blurry. They multiplied the remaining by 8 when finding backups. Then added 79 recovered files. Finally, multiplied by 5 for archival copies and added 73 more. Using 'dozens' as a measure, how many files does the photographer ultimately have?
w10_T4_009002: Sarah had 21 dollars. She added 43 dollars from her paycheck in the morning. Then 22 dollars from a side gig in the afternoon. She subtracted 14 dollars for gas. By evening, she received 38 dollars as a gift. Finally, she found 7 dollars in an old pocket. Comparing Sarah's money to Marcus's amount, how much does Sarah have in total?
w10_T4_009005: A factory had 16 machines running. They added 66 more new units. They multiplied the total by 9 for a productivity calculation. Then subtracted 589 due to maintenance shutdowns. They multiplied by 7 to project weekly output. Then by 9 again for a quarterly estimate. Adding the machines to the final tally, how many machines are counted in the system?
w10_T4_009006: A storage unit had 30 boxes. They added 25 boxes from a donation. Then removed 5 damaged boxes. They subtracted 46 boxes sold at auction. The remaining was divided in half. Finally, they multiplied by 8 for inventory projection. Between Michael (who manages storage) and Lisa (who tracks donations), how many boxes are accounted for?
w10_T4_009007: A truck started with 150 packages. In the morning, they added 7 packages. Then removed 118 at the first stop. By afternoon, they added 11 more packages. They removed 43 packages at the second stop. Finally, 6 packages were damaged and removed. Using twice the figure, how many packages does the truck have now?
w10_T4_009010: A supplier had 227 widgets. They added 61 widgets in a shipment. Then 59 more in another delivery. They subtracted 61 widgets that were returned. Finally, 14 widgets were added as replacements. A store owner ordered 350 widgets last month, but this was a separate transaction. What is the final count of widgets in inventory?
w10_T4_009011: A manager had 178 reports. They subtracted 46 outdated reports. Then added 59 new reports from the team. They added 77 more reports from a partner firm. Finally, 15 reports were added for the new quarter. Considering this is double the typical volume, how many reports does the manager have?
w10_T4_009013: A classroom had 29 desks. They multiplied by 6 for a conference setup. Then by 2 again for a larger regional event. They added 58 temporary desks for the event. Finally, they subtracted 253 desks that were moved to storage. In terms of seating capacity, how many desks remain?
w10_T4_009019: A construction site had 146 boxes of supplies. They multiplied by 5 for a major project phase. Then by 9 for the full-scale operation. Then by 6 for multiple team assignments. They subtracted 31756 boxes used in construction. Finally, 3735 more boxes were removed during cleanup. Considering one work crew used these supplies, how much was left?
w10_T4_009020: A printer had 190 reams of paper. They doubled the stock. Then added 19 reams from a new order. They subtracted 385 reams used in printing. Finally, they multiplied by 7 for weekly usage projections. Using the word 'twice', how much paper is in the final projection?
